name: Gena Liévano
bio_summary: One of the most promising international conductors, whose music leaves a profound trace in audiences.
bio_full:
Venezuelan conductor born in Caracas in 1998, Gena began her musical training at a very young age with her mother, a pianist. At ten, she joined the El Sistema program, where she learned to play the oboe and performed with numerous orchestras. In 2013, she was appointed Stage Manager for the Primo Casale opera company, with which she participated in a dozen operatic productions.

In 2015, Gena moved to Paris to continue her oboe studies and begin her conducting studies. After obtaining a Master's degree in Musicology from the Sorbonne University, three diplomas in musical studies, and a State diploma, she has dedicated herself fully to conducting since 2020.

Gena has participated in numerous masterclasses in France, the United Kingdom, Greece, the Czech Republic, and the Netherlands. He has had the opportunity to receive guidance from leading figures in conducting, such as Bertrand de Billy, Sian Edwards, Nicolas Pasquet, Johannes Schlaefli, Claire Gibault, Marc Korovitch, Claire Levacher, Alice Farnham, Martin Sieghart, and Michalis Economou. He also served as an assistant to Cyril Diederich (Barber of Seville and La Traviata), John Fiore (Kattenburg Competition), and Guillaume Bourgogne (Lausanne Society for Contemporary Music).

In 2022, he founded Anima, an orchestra and opera company, with a professional focus, which performs regularly in France and Spain. Since its inception, the ensemble has premiered a dozen works, including the five-act opera Blackbeard, which will be revived at the Massy Opera House in 2026.

She was the first guest conductor to lead the University of Alicante Philharmonic Orchestra in the summer of 2025.

Gena holds a master's degree in orchestral conducting from the Haute École de Musique de Lausanne in Switzerland and was awarded the Prix Tremplin by the Leenards-HEMU Foundation in 2025.
